instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Confess Around Them
cards.instruction: Use partial admissions to make a reciprocal confession feel like the only missing piece.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I changed the meeting time. Did you change the room?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You changed the time?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Yes. That's my half of why nobody met.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why didn't you tell me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I should have. Now tell me where your half of the meeting went.

cards.title: It Was Foreshadowed
cards.instruction: Turn the failure into a planned turning point by returning to earlier details that now appear to predict it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. The collapsed cake was foreshadowed by that first wobble.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You ignored the wobble.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I allowed the audience to discover its significance.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There is no cake now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. The empty stand pays off the warning beautifully.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the fallen tent for a moment. Remember the loose peg I pointed out? This is the turning point I was preparing you for.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You were supposed to hammer it in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you'd have missed what that little warning meant. Look at the whole roof now; you can see why I singled it out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can see we're getting soaked. Can we put it back up?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Start with that peg, and I'll tell you when it's deep enough. We needed the roof down before everyone understood the opening warning.

cards.title: Be Right in Retrospect
cards.instruction: Perform certainty by reinterpreting every surprise as something your earlier words were obviously predicting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When I said the evening would flow, I was plainly describing this kitchen flood. You may stop looking surprised.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You meant the conversation would flow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And what are we talking about? Water. Put that beside my original words before you dispute the forecast.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You didn't predict a burst pipe. Help me turn the water off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You take the valve; I'll clear the doorway. Once it stops flowing, you can tell me which part of my description was inaccurate.

cards.title: Reverse the Score
cards.instruction: Turn each apparent loss into a new category of victory, then invite comparison on those changing terms.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Last in the race, first in appreciating the route. Beat that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a speed contest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. A narrow category. How many wildflowers did you notice?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I noticed the finish line.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I also win for variety of attention.

cards.title: Return to the First Hope
cards.instruction: Return to an early hope after every setback, expanding its meaning until the whole scene seems to fulfill it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're going to look at this cottage properly. We wanted somewhere to belong; start by showing me where it leaks.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The whole roof needs replacing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll choose every tile. Bring me the roof estimate before you show me a house somebody else has finished.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That estimate could take all our savings.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then put the savings beside it and let's see. We were saving for a home; I want to know what that money can make ours, not how long we can keep looking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the concert chairs where they are. We promised to bring this village together, and we're starting on time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The power's out. Nobody will hear the microphones.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then move the singers in among the chairs. I'll give the first note; everyone can join without a microphone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Half the audience has gone home to fetch torches.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave their places ready and start with the people here. When they come back, bring them down the middle with the lights. They've found another way to join in.
